writeup.headline: Nutanix rates Buy on a net-cash balance sheet, strong cash margins, re-accelerating growth and firm price trend.
writeup.thesis: Nutanix scores 75, a Buy, with its strongest support from the balance sheet (98), valuation (88) and trend (81) factors. The company holds net cash, with cash at 1.75 times debt, and turns sales into cash well: gross margin is 86.8% and FCF margin 29.5%, though operating margin is a thinner 9.6%. Growth scores 68 on TTM revenue growth of 12.4%, with latest-quarter revenue growth of 15.9% year on year as growth sped up by 5.9 pp from the previous quarter. Against its own history, valuation sits near the middle of its own history overall, with P/FCF cheaper than at 38 of the last 50 month-ends and P/S near the middle of the last 50 month-ends (cheaper than at 24, more expensive than at 25). The shares trade at a price 39.0% above its 200-day average and 2.6% below its 52-week high, while news risk is a neutral 52.
key_risks: Stock-based compensation equals 12.5% of revenue, so GAAP operating margin of 9.6% lags cash profitability.
After a run that left shares 63.9 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, the price could give back gains if growth disappoints.
The CEO, CFO and a director made sizable sales in early October with no insider purchases, though under 10b5-1 plans.
The DOJ procurement investigation and the stayed Tessell suit remain unresolved background matters.
The commercial chief's departure could disrupt customer and partner relationships despite an advisory agreement.
what_would_change: Strong Buy is 5 points away: continued revenue acceleration lifting the growth score, or better operating margin lifting quality, could get there.
A fall to Hold needs a drop of 11 points, for example from growth slowing back down alongside a break in the price trend.
Negative news on the DOJ investigation, guidance or further insider selling would weigh on the news risk score.
A sharp rise in multiples against its own history would erode the valuation score.
